messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatiotemporal model: fixed effect specification and random effect AR1 with replicates
parts:
Can you be more specific about what you mean by replicates?
It doesn't make sense to replicate the "group part" of a model. Either the whole spatial-temporal model has multiple replicates, or only a single one.

Finn

Finn

parts:
dear Finn,
I am doing some exploratory analysis to find a credible model on one observational study on apples. I am looking for the diameter (DIAMETRO_MEDIO, response variable) vs. DOY (day of the year) and elevation (QUOTA, covariate). As you can see from the image i attached you the response is non-linear and the the different cultivar (VARIETA, covariate) have different speed of growth (and this is credible),

The model plotted (lines) is one of the many I tried
formula = DIAMETRO_MEDIO ~ 1 + ... + f(DOY, model="rw2", cyclic=FALSE, diagonal= 0.0001, scale.model= TRUE, replicate= VARIETA.idx)

and it seems to fit well my data and to be realistic at the same time.
Now, since I have the coordiantes of the sampling points I started to wonder to fit a spatiotemporal model
 - with the 'rw2', the replicate on VARIETA, and the spatial dependency - in just one shot, 
i.e. to have a different spatiotemporal field for each VARIETA
I hope to have been clearer, I am just trying to 'squeeze' the most from my data, 
so any help, hint or example is appreciated even if 'disruptive' !

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatiotemporal model: fixed effect specification and random effect AR1 with replicates
parts:
Quick note:
1) The f()-parameters "model" and "control.group" define a space-time model.
2) The first argument to f(), plus the parameters "group" and "replicate" determine where the model is to be evaluated.

In your earlier code you had "replicate" as a list member for control.group, which doesn't match the above.

Finn
